description.narrative: Detta icke-öronmärkta stöd till kontoret för FN:s högkommissarie för mänskliga rättigheter (OHCHR) i Colombia bygger på flera tidigare stöd till OHCHR, varav det senaste med ID-nummer 55190033. Programmets mål är följande: (i) Stärka rättsstatsprincipen och ansvarsskyldighet för kränkningar av de mänskliga rättigheterna; (ii) Förbättra och skydda det medborgerliga utrymmet och folkets deltagande; (iii) Öka jämlikhet och motverka diskriminering; (iv) Integrera mänskliga rättigheter i hållbar utveckling; (v) Tidig varning, förebyggande och skydd av mänskliga rättigheter i konflikt- och osäkerhetssituationer; och (vi) Öka genomförandet av resultaten från de internationella mekanismerna för mänskliga rättigheter. Ett jämställdhetsperspektiv kommer att integreras i stödet.

The non-earmarked support to the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in Colombia is for its Comprehensive Support Programme. The support builds upon several earlier contributions to OHCHR, the latest of which with ID-number: 55190033. The Programme’s objectives are: (i) Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations; (ii) Enhancing and Protecting Civic Space and People’s Participation; (iii) Enhancing equality and countering discrimination; (iv) Integrating human rights in sustainable development; (v) Early warning, prevention, and protection of human rights in situations of conflict and insecurity; and (vi) Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms’ outcomes. A gender perspective will be mainstreamed throughout the Programme.

OHCHR is a longlasting partner to Swedish cooperation. Their focus on protecting the enactment of Human Rights, serving as vocals to marginalised communities and supporting public institutions and duty bearers to duly comply with their democratic responsibilities is crucial to advance sustainable societies and efforts to achieve peace.
In Colombia, this unearmarked support contributes to OHCHR's overarching mandate All Human Rights for All. The Agency's Annual work plan operates under a series of tailored results, adapted to the country's circumstances and main issues that deter rightsholders' rights claims.
The following results cover the achievements OHCHR's work in Colombia that will continue to be supported by Sweden during the next four years:
a. Increased effectiveness of prevention and protection mechanisms and measures for civil society actors, including human rights defenders and other actors related to the peace process.
b. Relevant institutions and programs at the national, regional and local level incorporate a human rights based approach, especially in terms of participation and accountability in public policies resulting from peace processes and implementation of accords.
c. All actors involved in peace processes and implementation of accords increasingly recognize and comply with international human rights standards and humanitarian law and provide greater protection of civilians d. Transitional justice mechanisms provide increased accountability for conflict related violations.
e. The Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Defence, General Command of Military Forces, the National Police, the Procurator Generals Office and the Ombudsman´s Office act proactively to prevent human rights violations and to enhance their response when such violations occur.
f. Increased degree of implementation of the national action plan on business and human rights, including the involvement of the institutions responsible for economic and investment policies and of territorial entities.
g. Prioritized sectoral policies contribute to addressing and preventing human rights violations in the context of the justice system (addressing a. the restrictions of the military criminal justice on Hu man Rights violations b. coordination between ordinary jurisdiction, special indigenous jurisdiction and transitional jurisdiction).
h. The Social Prosperity Agency, the Illicit Crop Substitution Division, the National Land Agency, the Rural Development Agency and the Territorial Renovation Agency increasingly adopt and implement legislation, policies and strategies on poverty, land and housing in conformity with human rights standards.
i. Human Rights defenders, victims, ethnic peoples, women and LGBTI people increasingly participate in decision making processes affecting them.
j. National Institutions, namely the Ombudsman's Office, the Ministry of Interior, the Procurator General´s Office, the Ministry of Environment, the National Police and the Presidential Office for Women's Equity, more effectively combat discrimination against ethnic peoples, women and LGBTI people.

description.narrative:
Throughout 2024 and the first quarter of 2025, OHCHR Colombia continued its work to increase understanding and awareness of violence against human rights and environmental defenders in Colombia. In line with the priorities set by Sida's reform agenda, the following are examples of the most important results:
-They published the Annual Report on Human Rights in Colombia for the year 2024. As highlighted findings, there is a decrease in the number of verified killings of human rights defenders in comparison to 2023. The same happens with the number of verified massacres and the number of victims of forced displacement. On the other hand, there is an increase in cases of recruitment of children by non-state armed actors, with a disproportionate impact on Indigenous and Afro-descendant children, and an increase in the number of victims of confinement. -Within the framework of COP16, the Office presented and publicized an informative note on the challenges faced by these defenders, which received wide media coverage and institutional endorsement. It signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Environment to strengthen a protection network in the Amazon, provided technical cooperation on the Ministry's protocols, worked with organizational processes for environmental protection. -In the area of Business and Human Rights (EyDH), the OHCHR has worked with the current Government to strengthen its knowledge in business and human rights, especially in promoting the development of a Baseline Line in businesses and human rights - the first in the country - which allows for better decision-making inputs. -A visit of the delegation of the Working Group on Business and Human Rights took place during the third quarter of 2024. They highlighted the enormous challenges Colombia faces in protecting and respecting human rights in the context of business and made some recommendations for improvement. -With the technical and operational support of the OHCHR, the National Administrative Department of Statistics (DANE) has strengthened its information and analysis tools to develop statistical operations that include the peasantry as a population subject to rights in upcoming censuses and national surveys. -More than 200 officials from government agencies involved in rural development were trained to strengthen their technical capacity on human rights and international standards on peasant rights and the right to land. This made it possible to recognize and integrate the peasant population approach in harmony with the ethnic approach in the relevant institutional processes. -The OHCHR has played a fundamental role in accompanying and advising both entities and organizational processes of indigenous and Afro-descendant peoples, facilitating their demand for and access to measures that protect their rights to territory and a healthy environment. -During 2024, the OHCHR also increased the capacities of women human rights defenders to better protect themselves against gender-based violence and advocate for the protection of their rights before public institutions. It facilitated the participation of women in the development of the Action Plan of the Comprehensive Guarantee Program for Women Defenders and improved their knowledge about this plan for its implementation in their territories.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
